newsitem.title: USA: Ben Franklin use of funds approved.
newsitem.headline: Ben Franklin use of funds approved.

text.p: Ben Franklin Retail Stores Inc said Monday the U.S. Bankruptcy Court in Chicago has approved, with the consent of the company's secured lenders, the use of up to $59 million in cash collateral through December 31, 1996.
The company said use of the funds would allow it to sell product while it develops its business plan to emerge from bankruptcy.
The company said it will use the funds for inventory purchases and other operating expenses.

"The availability of these funds gives us the ability to distribute product while we continue to develop our business plan that will permit us to emerge from bankruptcy as a smaller, yet more vigorous, wholesaling company," Robert Kendig, chief operating officer, said in a news release. "This business will focus on selling craft and general merchandise to our current franchise and wholesale customer base."
Use of the cash collateral will be monitored by its secured lenders, the company said.
The craft wholesaler and operator of variety and craft stores filed for protection under Chapter 11 of the U.S. Bankruptcy Code on July 26.
